correctness.rationale: The divisor Möbius incidence matrix is integral unimodular and transforms the reduced Ramanujan matrix into D-1 b^T. The stated local relation d x_d=w solves the local cokernel: outside n it is cyclic of order ℓ^νℓφ(n); inside n, elimination of unit divisors, a unit Möbius coefficient and a high-power splitting yield exactly the claimed multiset. The determinant and modular ranks follow. Exhaustive determinantal-divisor enumeration for 2<=n<=30, determinant calculations for 2<=n<=150 and 1192 modular rank checks pass. Finite checks support but do not prove the universal claim.

originality.rationale: The previously recorded reduced-principal Smith classification for squarefree moduli is explicitly excluded from the novel part. Examined primary full texts cover supercharacter identities (Fowler–Garcia–Karaali 2012), determinant of a full Ramanujan divisor matrix (Schlage-Puchta 2021), and orthogonality/representation-theoretic use of a full divisor table (Shareshian–Sundaram 2023); none of the inspected statements gives the complete integer Smith invariants for nonsquarefree n. Targeted literature and database searches for aliases, local modules, principal deletion, and stronger coverage did not find an equivalent claim; residual broader-source risk remains. The new a>=2 prime-power torsion classification is not logically implied by any found earlier squarefree statement.
residual_risks: An unlocated result on integer Smith normal forms of all Ramanujan supercharacter tables or general divisor-incidence rank-one perturbations could specialize to this all-modulus theorem.
The squarefree specialization is covered by a previous result and is expressly not claimed as a new contribution.

value.rationale: This complete infinite natural arithmetic-matrix classification determines every prime-power component of the finite cokernel and all finite-field ranks. It substantially extends the covered squarefree case to arbitrary prime powers and mixed moduli, including a nontrivial interaction h=νℓφ(m) which raises a unique maximal local elementary divisor; determinant alone cannot detect that structure.
